objectives.description: The Sovereignty of God: God the Creator (Gen. 1; 2); God the Controller of the universe.
Parental responsibility: Eli and Samuel (1 Sam. 2:11-36, 3:1-18, 4:10-22, 8:1-5).
Consequences of Saul's disobedience (1 Sam. 15:1-26, 16:14-23, 31:1-13).
Submission to the will of God: David's submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26); David's sin, repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 12:15-25).
Making decisions: Solomon's wisdom (1 Kings 3:3-28, 4:29-34, 5:1-12, 8); the unwise decision of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23, 11:1-13, 12:1-20).
Supremacy of God: religious tensions during Ahab's reign (1 Kings 16:29-34, 17:1-7, 18:1-19); Elijah at Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:17-46).
Greed and its effects: Ahab (1 Kings 21:1-29); Gehazi (2 Kings 5).
Religious reforms: the reign of King Josiah (2 Kings 22, 23:1-30).
Concern for one's nation: the condition of the nation (2 Kings 24, 25:1-17); response to the state of the nation (Neh. 1, 2:9-20, 4; Ezra 1, 4, 5:1-2, 6:13-22, 7:1-10).
Faith in God: faith and courage (Dan. 3); faith and power (Dan. 6).
Nature of God: true religion and social justice — Amos (Amos 2:6-8, 4, 5:1-24, 7:10-17, 8); God's divine love — Hosea (Hos. 1, 2, 3, 6).

strands.name: Themes from the Synoptic Gospels and Acts

subStrands.name: Synoptic Gospels and Acts of the Apostles

objectives.description: Baptism and temptation of Jesus: the Baptism (Matt. 3:13-17, Mark 1:9-11, Luke 3:21-22); the Temptation (Matt. 4:1-11, Mark 1:12-13, Luke 4:1-13).
Jesus' teaching on forgiveness (Matt. 6:12, 14-15, 18:21-35).

The trials of Jesus: Jesus at Gethsemane (Matt. 26:36-56, Mark 14:32-52); Peter's denials (Matt. 26:69-75, Mark 14:66-72, Luke 22:54-62); condemnation of Jesus (Matt. 26:47-75, Mark 14:53-72, Luke 22:66-71, 23:1-12).
The crucifixion, burial and resurrection of Jesus: crucifixion and burial (Matt. 27:32-66, Mark 15:16-47, Luke 23:26-56); the Resurrection (Matt. 28:1-10, Mark 16:1-14, Luke 24:1-35).
Fellowship in the early church (Acts 1:15-26, 2:41-47, 4:32-37, 5:1-11, 6:2-6).
The Holy Spirit and the mission to the Gentiles: the Holy Spirit at Pentecost (Acts 2); mission to the Gentiles (Acts 9, 11:1-18).
Opposition to the gospel message (Acts 4:1-31, 5:17-42, 6:8-9, 7:1-10, 12:1-24).
The Epistle of James: faith and works (Jas. 1:2-27, 2:14-26); impartiality (Jas. 2:1-13); effective prayers (Jas. 1:2-8, 5:13-18).
The Epistle of 1 Peter: good citizenship (1 Pet. 2:13-17); Christians living among non-Christians (1 Pet. 2:1-25); interpersonal relationship among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-11).
